name: AWS Glue
sku: AWS Glue ETL jobs, Data Catalog, workflows and Data Quality.

ingest.batch-extract.note: A data integration service that connects to more than 70 data sources on premises and on AWS and loads them into data lakes.

transform.code-transform.note: ETL jobs run on a serverless, Apache Spark-based engine, authored visually in Glue Studio, in notebooks, or as edited scripts.

transform.stream-processing.note: Streaming ETL cleans and transforms data in transit so it is available in the target store within seconds.

orchestrate.scheduling.note: Workflows can start on a schedule, including custom cron expressions, or on demand.

orchestrate.dependency-dag.note: Triggers chain jobs and crawlers into dependency graphs that the console displays as a workflow graph with per-step run status. It orchestrates Glue components only.

orchestrate.event-triggers.note: A workflow can start on an Amazon EventBridge event or a batch of events, such as a new object arriving in S3.

bands.note: The Data Catalog is a centralised metadata repository, populated by crawlers that infer schemas, and queryable by Athena, EMR and Redshift Spectrum.

A Kinesis or Kafka/MSK streaming source used by a Glue streaming ETL job can be registered as a Data Catalog table, the same catalog store used for data at rest. For Kinesis this is optional (a job can read the stream directly instead); for Kafka a table has to be created by hand.

Glue Data Quality evaluates rules written in DQDL, with 25+ built-in rule types, recommended rules and a quality score. It runs inside ETL jobs to filter bad data before it loads and against cataloged tables at rest.

Machine learning detects anomalies and hard-to-spot quality issues from statistics gathered over time. Anomaly detection reached general availability in August 2024, and support for cataloged tables was added in July 2026.
Jobs are monitored with automated tooling, job run insights, CloudTrail and the Spark UI.

Schema Registry lets producers and consumers on Kafka, MSK, Kinesis Data Streams, Managed Flink and Lambda agree a schema, with 8 compatibility modes checked on every new version so an incompatible change is rejected, not silently accepted. Serverless and free to use.

The Detect PII transform in Glue Studio finds sensitive entities in a job's data and can redact, partially redact or SHA-256 hash them, inside batch or streaming ETL jobs. Effective only where a job is built to include the transform, not applied automatically to every job.

presentation.tagline: Serverless data integration: Spark ETL jobs, a metadata catalog and workflows.

cost.note: Standard ETL is $0.44/DPU-hour (Flex, for jobs that can start late, is $0.29); a few small jobs running occasionally at the 2-DPU minimum.
Regular daily jobs at the commonly-needed 3-5 DPUs each, several jobs a day.
Many jobs at higher DPU allocations. One documented real pipeline went from $0.66 for its first run to $5,000+/month six months into production.
